The duplicated runtime was a download cost. Each remote entry carried its own copy of `@module-federation/runtime-core`, so a page loaded that copy once per app. The app shell now publishes one copy on globals, and remotes read it from there. The change is ticket **O3-5873**, and the implementing commit is most likely PR #1853, though I matched that by file path rather than by message.

**Why it was a problem**

The changeset states the cost. Remote entries no longer embed their own copy of `runtime-core`, so a page downloads it once rather than once per app. On `@openmrs/esm-login-app`, a production remote entry dropped from about 85 kB to about 32 kB raw (about 26 kB to 9.7 kB gzipped). That makes the embedded runtime about 53 kB of the 85 kB, which matches the roughly two-thirds share in your question. The changeset does not describe a failure beyond the bytes, so I'm not claiming a runtime bug.
(openmrs-esm-core/.changeset/mf-runtime-shipped-once.md:8-14)

**What the app shell does now**

- The app shell builds with `experiments.provideExternalRuntime: true`. Module Federation then publishes `runtime-core` as `_FEDERATION_RUNTIME_CORE`, and the app shell's `optimization` settings apply to every app. (openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/rspack.config.js:489-502)
- `publishFederationRuntime()` also publishes `@module-federation/sdk` and `@module-federation/error-codes` as globals. It logs an error if `_FEDERATION_RUNTIME_CORE` is missing, which catches a mis-built shell. (openmrs-esm-core/packages/shell/esm-app-shell/src/federation-runtime.ts:16-42)
- Remotes build with `experiments.externalRuntime: true`, and an `ExternalsPlugin` maps the SDK and error codes to those globals. (openmrs-esm-core/packages/tooling/rspack-config/src/index.ts:471-484, 527-542)
- `@module-federation/runtime` and `webpack-bundler-runtime` stay bundled in each remote. They cache a federation instance at module scope, so sharing them would break remotes with RUNTIME-010. That is the roughly 14 kB that remains per remote.

I did not verify where `publishFederationRuntime()` is called, and I did not check the webpack config's matching block. The changeset also makes apps and app shells version-locked: a new remote refuses to start under an older shell.

8: (feat) O3-5873: Ship the Module Federation runtime once, from the app shell
9: 
10: Remote entries no longer embed their own copy of `@module-federation/runtime-core`; the app shell
11: publishes it on a global and remotes read it from there, so a page downloads it once rather than once per
12: app. Measured on `@openmrs/esm-login-app`, a production remote entry drops from ~85 kB to ~32 kB raw
13: (~26 kB to ~9.7 kB gzipped); the remainder is per-build federation glue plus the ~14 kB of runtime that
14: has to stay per remote.
15: 
16: Both shared configs now build with `@module-federation/enhanced` rather than the bundlers' built-in
17: Module Federation plugins, which also brings the webpack path onto the Module Federation 2.0 runtime.
18: Webpack-built remote entries grow as a result — ~8.7 kB to ~23 kB raw on the same app — because they
19: previously shipped a classic container with no runtime at all. Neither config emits an `mf-manifest.json`
20: or federated type declarations, as before.
21: 
22: **This is a breaking change for apps and app shells upgraded separately.** An app built with this version
23: of `@openmrs/rspack-config`, `@openmrs/webpack-config` or the `openmrs` CLI requires an app shell of this
24: version or newer, and refuses to start under an older one with an error in the browser console naming
25: itself. Apps built with older tooling keep working in the new app shell, so a distribution can mix old
26: apps with a new app shell but not the reverse. An app and its app shell should also be built against the
27: same Module Federation minor; a mismatch logs a warning rather than failing the load, because minor skew
28: usually works and a changed runtime helper only sometimes breaks shared-dependency de-duplication. There
29: is deliberately no machine-readable compatibility field yet — the app shell's own version is the contract.
30: 
31: One consequence worth knowing: because every remote now shares the app shell's `runtime-core`, that
32: build's identifier and its `experiments.optimization` settings apply to every app's federation instance.
33: The app shell therefore sets only `target: 'web'`, which is true of every app in a distribution.
